filters.name: abs
filters.description: Returns the absolute value of a number.

filters.name: capitalize
filters.description: Capitalizes the first character of a string and makes all other characters lowercase.

filters.name: center
filters.description: Centers a string in a field of a given width by padding it with a character on both sides.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: The total width of the resulting string

parameters.name: fillChar
parameters.description: Optional character to use for padding (default is space)

filters.name: default
filters.description: Returns a default value if the input is undefined. If the second parameter is true, also returns default for falsy values (0, false, empty string, etc).

parameters.name: defaultValue
parameters.description: The value to return if input is undefined

parameters.name: boolean
parameters.description: Optional flag to treat falsy values as undefined (default: false)

filters.name: dump
filters.description: Converts a value to a JSON string. Useful for debugging or outputting data structures.

parameters.name: indent
parameters.description: Optional number of spaces for indentation (for pretty-printing)

filters.name: escape
filters.description: Escapes HTML special characters (&, <, >, ', ") so they can be safely displayed in HTML without being interpreted as markup. Alias: e

filters.name: first
filters.description: Returns the first item from a sequence.

filters.name: float
filters.description: Converts a value to a floating point number. Returns 0.0 if conversion fails, unless a default is provided.

parameters.name: default
parameters.description: Optional default value if conversion fails (default: 0.0)

filters.name: forceescape
filters.description: Enforces HTML escaping by escaping already-escaped content. May result in double-escaping.

filters.name: indent
filters.description: Indents every line of a string. The first line and blank lines are not indented by default.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Number of spaces or a string to indent by

parameters.name: first
parameters.description: Whether to indent the first line (default: false)

parameters.name: blank
parameters.description: Whether to indent empty lines (default: false)

filters.name: int
filters.description: Converts a value to an integer. Returns 0 if conversion fails, unless a default is provided. The base (2-36) can be overridden for strings with prefixes like 0b, 0o, 0x.

parameters.name: default
parameters.description: Optional default value if conversion fails (default: 0)

filters.name: join
filters.description: Joins a list of strings with a separator. Can optionally extract an attribute from a list of objects.

parameters.name: separator
parameters.description: String to insert between items (default: empty string)

parameters.name: attribute
parameters.description: Optional attribute name to extract from objects before joining

filters.name: last
filters.description: Returns the last item from a sequence.

filters.name: length
filters.description: Returns the number of items in a container (list, string, object, etc).

filters.name: list
filters.description: Converts an iterable (string, object, etc) to a list.

filters.name: lower
filters.description: Converts a string to lowercase.

filters.name: nl2br
filters.description:
Replaces newline characters with HTML
tags.

filters.name: random
filters.description: Returns a random item from a sequence.

filters.name: reject
filters.description: Filters a sequence by rejecting items that pass a test. If no test is specified, falsy items are rejected.

filters.name: rejectattr
filters.description: Filters a sequence of objects by rejecting those where a specified attribute passes a test.

filters.name: replace
filters.description: Replaces all occurrences of a substring with another string. Optionally limit to the first N replacements.

parameters.name: new
parameters.description: The string to replace it with

filters.name: reverse
filters.description: Reverses a sequence or returns an iterator that reverses the order.

filters.name: round
filters.description: Rounds a number to a given precision. The rounding method can be 'common' (round half up), 'ceil' (always up), or 'floor' (always down).

filters.name: safe
filters.description: Marks a string as safe for direct output, bypassing HTML escaping. Use with caution!

filters.name: select
filters.description: Filters a sequence by selecting only items that pass a test. If no test is specified, truthy items are selected.

filters.name: selectattr
filters.description: Filters a sequence of objects by selecting those where a specified attribute passes a test.

filters.name: slice
filters.description: Slices an iterator and returns a list of lists containing those items. If you pass a second argument, it's used to fill missing values on the last iteration.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: The number of items per slice

parameters.name: fillValue
parameters.description: Optional value to pad the final slice if incomplete

examples.template: {% for items in [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] | slice(2) %}{{ items }}{% endfor %}

filters.name: string
filters.description: Converts an object to a string representation if it isn't already. Preserves Markup strings.

filters.name: striptags
filters.description: Removes HTML/XML tags from a string, leaving only the content inside.

parameters.name: preserve_linebreaks
parameters.description: Optional flag to preserve line breaks (default: false)

filters.name: title
filters.description: Returns a titlecased version of the string where the first character of each word is uppercase and remaining characters are lowercase.

filters.name: trim
filters.description: Strips leading and trailing characters from a string. By default removes whitespace.

filters.name: truncate
filters.description: Truncates a string to a specified length. By default, cuts at word boundaries and adds an ellipsis.

parameters.name: killwords
parameters.description: If true, cut the text at exactly length instead of at word boundaries (default: false)

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: String to append at the end (default: '...')

examples.template: {{ 'This is a long sentence.' | truncate(10, true) }}

filters.name: upper
filters.description: Converts a string to uppercase.

filters.name: urlencode
filters.description: Quotes data for use in a URL. For strings, escapes special characters. For dicts/iterables, creates a query string.

filters.name: urlize
filters.description: Converts URLs in text into clickable links. Works with http://, https://, www., mailto:, and email addresses.

parameters.name: trim_url_limit
parameters.description: Shorten displayed URL values to this length

filters.name: wordcount
filters.description: Counts the number of words in a string.

filters.name: wordwrap
filters.description: Wraps a string to the given width, breaking lines at word boundaries. Existing newlines are treated as paragraph breaks.

parameters.name: break_long_words
parameters.description: Break words longer than width (default: true)

filters.name: as_timezone
filters.description: Convert a datetime to a specified timezone.

filters.name: convert_from_epoch
filters.description: Convert an epoch timestamp to a datetime string.

filters.name: datedelta
filters.description: Add or subtract a time interval from a datetime.

filters.name: format_datetime
filters.description: Format a datetime using Luxon format tokens.

filters.name: parse_datetime
filters.description: Parse a datetime string with a specified format string.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Luxon format string to use for parsing (e.g., 'yyyy-MM-dd', 'MM/dd/yyyy HH:mm')

examples.template: {{ 'May 4, 2025 2:30 PM' | parse_datetime('MMMM d, yyyy h:mm a') }}

filters.name: time_delta
filters.description: Add a duration to a datetime (alias for datedelta).

filters.name: json
filters.description: Converts a value to a formatted JSON string. Objects and arrays are pretty-printed with 2-space indentation.

filters.name: reject_empty
filters.description: Rejects items from a list where the specified attribute is empty (null, undefined, empty array, or empty string).

parameters.name: attr
parameters.description: The attribute name to check for emptiness

examples.output: Items where entries is not null, undefined, [], or ''

filters.name: map
filters.description: Extracts an attribute from each item in a list, or applies a transformation.

parameters.name: attribute
parameters.description: The attribute name to extract from each item. Supports dot notation for nested attributes.

filters.name: unique
filters.description: Returns only unique values from a list. Optionally deduplicate by a specific attribute.

parameters.name: attribute
parameters.description: Optional attribute name to use for uniqueness comparison.

filters.name: max
filters.description: Returns the maximum value from a list. Use attribute keyword to compare by object attribute.

filters.name: min
filters.description: Returns the minimum value from a list. Use attribute keyword to compare by object attribute.

filters.name: sum
filters.description: Sums values in a list. Use attribute keyword to sum by object attribute.

filters.name: groupby
filters.description: Groups a list of objects by an attribute. Returns list of {grouper, list} objects.

examples.template: {% for group in items | groupby('type') %}{{ group.grouper }}: {{ group.list | length }}{% endfor %}

filters.name: dictsort
filters.description: Sorts a dictionary by key or value, returning a list of [key, value] pairs.

parameters.name: case_sensitive
parameters.description: Whether sort is case sensitive (default: false)

examples.template: {% for k, v in mydict | dictsort %}{{ k }}: {{ v }}{% endfor %}

filters.name: batch
filters.description: Slices a list into batches of n items.

parameters.name: fill
parameters.description: Optional fill value for incomplete last batch

filters.name: sort
filters.description: Sort a list, optionally by attribute. Supports reverse and case_sensitive options.

parameters.name: attribute
parameters.description: Attribute to sort by (supports dot notation)

filters.name: count
filters.description: Returns the number of items in a list, string, or object. Alias for length.

filters.name: is_empty
filters.description: Returns true if the value is empty: "", [], {}, null, or undefined. Does not treat 0 or false as empty.

examples.output: no errors (when errors_html is "", [], {}, or none)

filters.name: deep_eq
filters.description: Deep equality comparison using JSON serialization. Useful for comparing arrays and objects, where Nunjucks == does reference equality. The preprocessor automatically rewrites == [] and == {} to use this filter.

filters.name: in_list
filters.description: Checks if a value is a member of a list using deep equality. Replaces the built-in "in" operator when the list contains [] or {} literals, which Nunjucks cannot match correctly. The preprocessor automatically rewrites "in [... [] ...]" to use this filter.

examples.template: {% if CTX.val not in [[], "", none] %}...{% endif %}
examples.output: (preprocessor rewrites to in_list automatically when [] is in the list)

filters.name: not_deep_eq
filters.description: Inverse of deep_eq. Used by the preprocessor to rewrite != [] and != {} comparisons.

filters.name: not_in_list
filters.description: Inverse of in_list. Used by the preprocessor to rewrite "not in" when the list contains [] or {} literals.

examples.template: {% if CTX.val not in [[], "", none] %}...{% endif %}

filters.name: regex_match
filters.description: Tests whether a value matches a regular expression pattern. Rewst-compatibility addition -- Rewst's own Jinja environment ships a regex_match(value, pattern) global that Kore had no equivalent for. NOT standard Jinja2 either (vanilla Jinja2 has no built-in regex support at all). Registered as a filter only -- Rewst's function-call syntax (regex_match(value, pattern)) does not work in Kore; ported templates must use filter syntax instead. Pattern is JS RegExp syntax, not Python's re module. null/undefined values are coerced to '' (simply fail to match) rather than thrown. Throws if pattern is missing/empty or not a valid regular expression.

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: Regular expression source (JS RegExp syntax). Required.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Optional JS RegExp flags, e.g. 'i' for case-insensitive matching (default: '')

filters.name: regex_extract_all
filters.description: Returns every full match of a pattern within a string, as an array. Unlike regex_match (boolean only), this actually extracts the matched text - lets a template pull repeated, structurally-identical chunks (e.g. every <ScriptSteps>...</ScriptSteps> block in an XML document) out of a larger string without a dedicated XML parser. The 'g' flag is added automatically if not already present in the given flags, since matching a repeated pattern implies wanting every occurrence, not just the first.

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: Regular expression source (JS RegExp syntax). Required.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Optional JS RegExp flags. 'g' is added automatically if missing (default: '')

examples.template: {% for block in CTX.log_text | regex_extract_all('ERROR:.*') %}{{ block }}{% endfor %}

filters.name: regex_groups
filters.description: Matches a pattern against a string once and returns its capture groups as an array, in order - or null if the pattern didn't match at all. Pairs with regex_extract_all: extract every repeated chunk first, then call regex_groups on each one to pull out several named fields in a single pass instead of one regex_match call per field. A capture group that matched but captured nothing (e.g. an alternation branch for a self-closing tag) comes back as '' rather than undefined, so template code doesn't need | d('') on every field.

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: Regular expression source with one or more capture groups. Required.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Optional JS RegExp flags. 'g' is NOT added automatically - only the first match is used (default: '')

filters.name: xml_unescape
filters.description: Decodes the five predefined XML/HTML entities (< > & " ') back to their literal characters - the inverse of the standard escape/e filter. Generic text-processing utility, not tied to any one data source. & is decoded last so a doubly-escaped entity like &lt; correctly becomes < rather than being unescaped all the way to <. null/undefined become ''.

filters.name: merge_dict
filters.description: Returns a NEW object combining a base object with updates (updates win on key conflicts). Paired with a preprocessor rewrite so {% do obj.update({...}) %} works the same way {% do list.append(x) %} already does, since plain objects have no native in-place update method.

parameters.name: updates
parameters.description: Object whose keys/values are merged into the base object

examples.output: (preprocessor rewrites automatically to {% set computer = computer | merge_dict({'type': 'Server'}) %})

filters.name: from_json_string
filters.description: Parses a JSON-formatted string into a real array/object so it can be looped over, indexed, or reshaped within the same template. Inverse of | json / | auto_json. Non-string input passes through unchanged. Throws if the string is not valid JSON.

examples.template: {% set data = ps_result | from_json_string %}{% for item in data %}{{ item.Folder }}{% endfor %}

filters.name: sql_escape
filters.description: Escapes a value for safe embedding in a raw SQL string literal (backslash-then-quote escaping). The sqlquery plugin task executes its query input completely verbatim with no parameterization, so any dynamic value going into hand-built SQL text must be escaped this way first. null/undefined become an empty string.

filters.name: ps_escape
filters.description: Escapes a value for safe embedding in a PowerShell single-quoted string literal. Only doubles single quotes - unlike sql_escape, backslashes are left untouched since PowerShell single-quoted strings treat them as literal, inert characters (no escape sequences at all).

filters.name: to_html
filters.description:
Converts plain text into safe HTML for use in an email/HTML context: escapes HTML special characters (&, <, >, ", ') first, then converts line breaks (\r\n, \r, or \n) to
, so multi-line plain-text content actually renders with line breaks instead of running together as one line, which a bare newline does not do inside real HTML. null/undefined become an empty string.

filters.name: bool
filters.description: Converts a value to a real boolean. The string literals "true"/"false" (any case, e.g. "True", "FALSE", surrounding whitespace trimmed) are parsed as the boolean they name -- this is the case that matters for form-submitted values, where a checkbox/select often arrives as the string "false" rather than a real boolean, and generic truthiness would wrongly treat that non-empty string as true. Any other string falls back to generic truthiness (non-empty = true). Other falsy values: false, 0, 0.0, '', null, undefined, empty arrays/objects.

examples.output: false (when the form submitted the string "false")
